name: stackyard
description: Free, open-source app for Windows and macOS that finds every SDK and toolchain on your machine (Flutter, Node.js, Android SDK, Xcode simulators, Java, Python, .NET, Gradle), shows which projects use each version, fixes broken setups in one click and frees disk space.
readme_summary: Stackyard is a free, open-source desktop application for Windows and macOS that helps developers manage their software development kits (SDKs) and toolchains. It identifies all installed SDKs, tracks which projects use them, and provides one-click solutions to fix broken setups and free up disk space by removing unused versions.
key_features: Finds all installed SDKs and toolchains (Flutter, Node.js, Android SDK, Xcode, Java, Python, .NET, Gradle, etc.)
Shows which projects use each SDK version
Fixes broken development setups with one-click solutions
Frees up disk space by identifying and removing unused SDKs and toolchains
Supports version managers like FVM, nvm, fnm, and Volta
Installs SDKs and CLIs from publisher release feeds with integrity checks
Manages environment variables (PATH, JAVA_HOME, GOROOT)
Identifies and fixes common environment issues (e.g., broken JAVA_HOME)
primary_use_case: Managing and cleaning up multiple SDKs and toolchains on a developer's machine to optimize disk space and fix environment configuration issues.
cover_image_prompt: A digital librarian meticulously organizing a vast library of software development kits (SDKs) and toolchains. The librarian, representing Stackyard, is shown sorting glowing, distinct icons for Flutter, Node.js, Android, and Xcode into labeled shelves. Some shelves are overflowing, indicating unused versions, while others are neatly organized, showing projects linked to specific SDKs via glowing threads. A 'Clean Up' button hovers near a pile of dusty, unused SDK boxes, ready to be cleared. The background is a clean, modern workspace with subtle code snippets on a monitor. The overall mood is organized and efficient, with a bright, clear color palette. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clarity and intuitive representation of digital organization.

name: thehumanbox
description: Free civilization sandbox in your browser. Tribes invent their own languages, cultures and wars, from stone age to computers. Rust → WASM, no server, no LLM.
readme_summary: The Human Box is a free, browser-based civilization sandbox simulation written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly. It allows users to observe or influence autonomous tribes as they develop languages, cultures, technologies, and engage in complex societal interactions from the stone age to the computer age, all running client-side without a server or LLM.
key_features: Autonomous tribal development (language, culture, cities, religion, war, treaties)
Runs entirely in the browser via WebAssembly (no server, no LLM)
Client-side simulation with local saves and export functionality
Rust-based simulation engine
Optional desktop application via Electron
Procedural generation of languages and cultures
45 distinct historical eras
primary_use_case: To provide a free, accessible, and client-side civilization simulation sandbox where users can observe or interact with emergent societal development.
cover_image_prompt: A vibrant, stylized diorama depicting a miniature world within a transparent, glowing cube labeled 'The Human Box'. Inside, tiny, diverse tribes are shown at different stages of development: one group is crafting stone tools, another is building rudimentary huts, a third is engaged in a peaceful exchange of goods, and a fourth is operating a small, early computer. Wisps of digital energy flow between the tribes, representing emergent culture and language. The background is a clean, abstract gradient suggesting a digital space. The overall mood is one of creation and emergent complexity. 3D isometric illustration style with clear, soft lighting and a focus on the intricate details of the miniature civilizations.

name: gsc
description: GSC — verified remediation engine: SAST that proves exploits (PoC), verifies fixes (Proof-of-Fix), and self-heals CI. Apache 2.0 + Commercial.
readme_summary: GSC is a self-learning AppSec platform that automates the process of detecting, proving, and fixing security vulnerabilities in code. It generates runnable proof-of-concepts for findings, verifies fixes through re-running exploits, and integrates into CI/CD pipelines for continuous security.
key_features: SAST, SCA, secrets, and IaC scanning with 69 detectors
Automated Proof-of-Concept (PoC) generation for findings
Proof-of-Fix verification to ensure vulnerabilities are actually resolved
Self-learning engine that re-scores detectors and deactivates noisy patterns
Prioritization based on exploitability (EPSS, CISA KEV, ExploitDB) rather than CVSS
BYO-LLM support for enhanced revalidation, with a fallback to regex-only mode
GitHub Action integration and MCP server for CI/CD and client integration
primary_use_case: Automating the detection, proof, and verification of code vulnerabilities within CI/CD pipelines to improve application security.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant digital alchemist in a futuristic laboratory, meticulously examining glowing code manuscripts. The alchemist uses a magnifying glass that reveals not just errors, but miniature, animated 'exploit simulations' within the code. For each validated exploit, the alchemist places a 'verified fix' stamp, causing the simulation to dissolve harmlessly. Surrounding the alchemist are shelves filled with 'knowledge scrolls' representing the self-learning aspect, and a small, integrated monitor displays the repository's name, 'GSC', alongside a progress bar indicating a secure CI pipeline. The style is a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, high-tech aesthetic and a color palette of blues, purples, and glowing accents.

name: bybit-ws
description: AI-Native Trading Engine — Bollinger Grid LONG/SHORT. REST API + MCP for AI agents. 24/7 automated trading on Bybit.
readme_summary: Bybit-WS is an AI-native trading engine designed for 24/7 automated trading on the Bybit futures market. It utilizes Bollinger Bands combined with a 9-metric AI scoring system for entry points, and incorporates advanced risk management and deposit protection features.
key_features: AI-Native Trading Engine
Bollinger Bands + AI Scoring for Entry
Automated LONG/SHORT Trading
Advanced Risk Management (Stop-loss, Take-profit, Trailing, DCA)
Deposit Protection (Circuit Breaker, BlackSwan, Anti-ludomania)
Self-Learning Market Classification (LSTM)
Backtesting and Paper Trading
RPC API and MCP Server for AI Agents
Telegram Alerts
primary_use_case: Automated, AI-driven cryptocurrency futures trading on Bybit with robust risk management.
cover_image_prompt: A sophisticated, AI-powered trading robot with glowing blue circuits, standing confidently on a digital representation of the Bybit exchange. The robot is actively managing multiple streams of data visualized as flowing ribbons of numbers and charts, some turning green (profits) and others red (losses). In the background, a dynamic Bollinger Bands indicator is clearly visible, with the robot's 'hand' precisely interacting with the bands to signal trade entries and exits. Small, subtle UI elements showing risk management metrics and AI scoring are integrated into the robot's design. The overall scene is futuristic and clean, emphasizing automated intelligence and market control. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a dark, high-tech color palette and neon accents.

name: watchstate
description: Self-hosted service to sync your plex, jellyfin and emby play state. without relying on 3rd-party external services.
readme_summary: WatchState is a self-hosted PHP service designed to synchronize playback progress across multiple media servers like Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby. It operates without relying on third-party services, offering features such as multi-user support, webhook event handling, and the ability to back up playback states.
key_features: Multi-users support via identities
Sync backends play state (many-to-many or one-way)
Backup backends play state into portable format
Receive webhook events from media backends
Find record issues with Media Health
Search backend metadata
Sync watch progress/play state via webhooks or scheduled tasks
primary_use_case: Synchronizing user playback state across different media server platforms (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby) in a self-hosted environment.
cover_image_prompt: A digital librarian meticulously organizing and cross-referencing glowing books from three distinct, ornate shelves labeled 'Plex', 'Jellyfin', and 'Emby'. The librarian is shown with a tablet displaying synchronized progress bars, indicating that a viewer's 'current page' is identical across all books, regardless of which shelf they originated from. Subtle data streams connect the books, symbolizing the synchronization. The background is a cozy, dimly lit study, with a small, stylized 'WatchState' logo subtly integrated into a wall plaque. The overall style is a warm, inviting 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clarity and a soft, digital glow.
